title: REPRODUCE-ONLY: CEGIS refinement feedback leaks the held-out acceptance rows (defect C)

inference_substrate.principle: The dominant compute is offline-arcade env stepping (13 roster games solved to L1 through their adapters by build_progress_window) plus pure-Python WorldModelVerifier scoring. NO LLM is loaded, no GGUF, no CUDA. Declaring the substrate explicitly is what stops the duration floor being applied from the wrong tier -- see CLAUDE.md Inference-Substrate Declaration Discipline.

solve_provenance.principle: No level, solve or reproduced_levels is claimed by this artifact at all. The offline dev twin was used purely as a source of REAL transition windows to measure an instrument against; declaring the weaker provenance is the honest label even when no solve claim is made.

verifier_is_oracle.principle: No verifier-value, moat or efficiency claim is made here. This artifact measures a MEASUREMENT defect in a gate, not a verifier's discriminative power.

random_seed.principle: Every engine and corpus in this reproduction is constructed deterministically (memorised transition tables, index-ordered subsets); there is no sampling. The seed is recorded so a third party can confirm determinism rather than assume it.

reproducibility_checksum.principle: SHA256 over the reproduction script plus the three shipped modules whose behaviour is being measured. If any of them changes, the numbers below must be re-derived rather than re-cited.

preconditions_checked.evidence: build_progress_window returned a window for 13/13 roster games
no llama_cpp / transformers / CUDA import on any path in this reproduction

question: Are the rows that GRADE acceptance (heldout_accuracy, last third, threshold 1.0) disjoint from the rows that SHAPE refinement (the mismatches rendered into refactor_prompt)?
answer: No. They overlap, deterministically, and the overlap is DELIVERED into the prompt string.

mechanism_traced_in_shipped_code.acceptance: arc_llm_reinduction.py:1535-1536 reads select_trusted_world_model(...).selected_score.heldout_accuracy and compares it to verifier_threshold (min_heldout_accuracy=1.0 at both live call sites, arc_competition_agent.py:6225 and :6362). select_trusted_world_model splits at arc_world_model_trust_energy.py:595 via _split_prefix_heldout -> last max(1, round(n/3)) rows.
mechanism_traced_in_shipped_code.refinement: arc_llm_reinduction.py:1585 builds WorldModelVerifier(list(transitions), hud_mask=hud_mask).score(selected.engine) -- the FULL corpus, prefix AND held-out -- with the shipped default max_mismatch=8, mismatches appended in index order, each carrying true_change=_delta(g0,g1), i.e. the OBSERVED next state.
mechanism_traced_in_shipped_code.delivery: line 1596 real_mismatches -> line 1496 proposer.refactor(game, _counterexample_result(ce)) -> refactor_prompt (arc_executable_world_model.py:3001) -> _bounded_mismatches(vr.mismatches, limit=5) -> the first FIVE mismatches, verbatim, in the prompt text.

exact_leak_law.why: mismatches are collected in INDEX order and prefix rows have lower indices than held-out rows, so prefix mismatches occupy the 5 render slots first. Prefix mismatches are exactly what an engine that is GOOD on the prefix does not have.

delivery_check.principle: Availability is not delivery. Every leak count below is obtained by PARSING the mismatch block back out of the rendered prompt STRING and mapping each true_change tuple to its row by that row's own unique changed cell -- never by trusting the mismatch's own `i` label.

A_real_window_shapes_measured.note: build_progress_window (WINDOW_K=12) on the exp5760/5764/5766 roster. These are the shapes the null was actually measured at -- they are NOT n=25.

B_leak_on_real_windows_prefix_perfect_ar.note: engine reproduces every prefix row exactly and no held-out row -- the regime the leak is claimed to be worst in.

C_leak_on_real_windows_floor_engine_arm.note: engine wrong on every row -- the regime exp5766's treated arm actually occupied. Leak still fires on SHORT corpora, where the 3-row prefix cannot fill the 5 render slots.

D_synthetic_sweep_at_the_live_agent_shap.note: n=25 is the live-agent corpus shape tabulated in the shipped _induce_transitions_k docstring for six captured games. prefix 17 / held-out 8 computed by calling _split_prefix_heldout, not by arithmetic.

G_adjacent_defect_induce_prompt_channel.finding: The induce prompt itself shows the held-out tail. At today's shipped default (_induce_transitions_k() -> None = ALL, since 2026-08-01) every changed transition is rendered with its delta; on the n=25 synthetic that is 8/8 held-out rows. Under the legacy cap the picture is corpus-dependent: the cap is changed[:k-2], so on the synthetic (25 changed rows) it renders rows 0-5 and leaks 0/8.
G_adjacent_defect_induce_prompt_channel.consequence: Fixing only the refinement-feedback channel does NOT restore purity on the current default: the acceptance rows were already shown, with answers, in round 1.

H_derived_incidence_on_the_real_exp5766_.derivation_disclosure: DERIVED, not directly measured: the exp5766 shard trims counterexamples, so per-round mismatch lists are unavailable. Computed by applying the exact leak law (validated 270/270 above) to each round's RECORDED prefix_accuracy and heldout_accuracy together with that game's DIRECTLY MEASURED window shape. Treat as an estimate with a known formula, not as a re-measurement.

design_i_prefix_only_refinement.cost: starved of counterexamples in exactly the regime the leak occurs

design_ii_third_never_touched_split.cost: the acceptance set shrinks to a handful of gradeable rows at the real corpus sizes
design_ii_third_never_touched_split.real_window_implication: at the measured n<=12 windows, halving the tail leaves 1-2 raw accept rows of which 0-1 are gradeable; on the four n<=4 games a three-way split is arithmetically impossible

recommendation: design (ii) -- a third, never-touched acceptance split -- but ONLY together with three non-optional companions; design (i) is rejected on measured grounds. See recommendation_detail.

recommendation_detail.why_not_i: prefix-only refinement was starved (ZERO counterexamples) on 9 of 9 real roster windows in the prefix-perfect arm -- the same 9 windows where the leak fires. It replaces a leaky loop with an inert one and would produce a second uninterpretable null. CEGIS with no counterexample is not CEGIS, and the in-code comment defending full-corpus scoring is right about that much.
recommendation_detail.why_ii: it preserves every counterexample the refinement loop wants (prefix + refine-tail) while making the acceptance rows unreachable by any prompt. The cost is gate PRECISION, which is a knob (grow the window), not a structural loss.
recommendation_detail.companion_1_gradeable_not_raw: the acceptance split must be counted in GRADEABLE rows -- level-up rows excluded -- or defect F reproduces inside the new split and worsens it.
recommendation_detail.companion_2_induce_prompt: the acceptance rows must also be withheld from _transitions_block / induce_prompt. Without this the fix is decorative on the current ALL-transitions default: the model already saw the acceptance rows with answers in round 1 (measured 8/8).
recommendation_detail.companion_3_undecidable_not_zero: when the corpus cannot supply a minimum number of gradeable acceptance rows, report the gate as UNDECIDABLE rather than 0.0. Today 4 of 13 roster games silently return 0.0 and reject a perfect engine.
recommendation_detail.fallback_for_tiny_corpora: at n<=5 a three-way split is impossible; there, prefix-only refinement is the only purity-preserving option and is NOT starved for a genuinely bad engine (measured: r11l 2 prefix mismatches, vc33 2, sp80 3, ft09 3 in the floor arm).
recommendation_detail.flag: CARNOT_ARC_CEGIS_ACCEPT_SPLIT, default OFF; OFF must reproduce the shipped trajectory byte-for-byte including the leak, ON enables the split. This IS a behaviour change (it moves which rows grade acceptance), so instrumentation-only exemption does not apply.

what_this_artifact_does_NOT_claim: That an LLM exploits the leak. Proving exploitation needs a live generator A/B; only the measurement defect is proven here.

That the leak caused the reported null. It did not: exp5766's refactor rounds sat on the floor (2 of 77 rounds above prefix_accuracy 0, max 0.125), so the prefix-perfect regime was largely unreached. The leak is a LATENT defect that bites once defect (A) is fixed -- plus a live one on the short corpora (cd82, lp85), where it fires even for a floor engine.
Any level, solve or reproduced_levels claim.
That n=25 is the offline harness shape. It is not: the measured harness windows are n=3..12.
methodology_note: heldout_accuracy values of exactly 1.0 and 0.0 appear throughout and are BY CONSTRUCTION, not capability claims: the engines are memorising lookup tables built to be exactly right or exactly wrong on chosen rows, which is the only way to isolate the index-ordering mechanism. The one substantive 0.0 is defect F, where a PERFECT engine scores 0.0 -- that is the finding, not an artefact.
n_samples_justification: 270 synthetic configurations (3 corpus shapes x 3 prefix-correctness patterns x every prefix-correct count x 2 held-out settings) plus 13 real roster windows x 3 engine arms = 39 real measurements. The claim is DETERMINISTIC (an exact index-ordering law), so the sample size is there to falsify the law across shapes, not to estimate a rate; the law held on 270/270.

F_adjacent_defect_unfalsifiable_acceptan.finding: On 4 of the 13 roster games the entire held-out tail is the single level-up transition, which WorldModelVerifier.score EXCLUDES from grading. n becomes 0, accuracy is n_correct/max(1,n)=0.0, and the gate rejects a PERFECT engine.
F_adjacent_defect_unfalsifiable_acceptan.verified_by: constructing a memorising engine that reproduces every observed transition exactly and reading select_trusted_world_model's own heldout_accuracy
F_adjacent_defect_unfalsifiable_acceptan.principle: missing is not zero -- an ungradeable acceptance set must report undecidable, not 0.0
